CVE-2026-129319.title: create-ecdh: computeSecret does not validate that the peer public key is on the curve (invalid-curve attack)
CVE-2026-129319.description: create-ecdh is a browserifiable implementation of Node.js crypto.createECDH. In versions 4.0.4 and below, the JavaScript implementation (browser.js, used by browser bundlers and on Node.js versions without a working native crypto.createECDH) did not validate peer public keys in ECDH.prototype.computeSecret or ECDH.prototype.setPublicKey. The peer point was multiplied by the local private key without checking that it was on the configured curve or in its prime-order subgroup. An attacker who can submit public keys to a party that reuses a static private key can perform an invalid-curve or small-subgroup attack and recover the private key modulo small factors, eventually recovering the full key via the Chinese Remainder Theorem. For the ed25519 and curve25519 curves, low-order points were also accepted, which could force a predictable shared secret. On modern Node.js, create-ecdh re-exports the native implementation, which is not affected. This issue is fixed in version 4.0.5.

CVE-2026-136508.title: MSDTC connections drop the connection's TLS and channel binding settings
CVE-2026-136508.description:
On Windows, when a connection takes part in a distributed transaction, psqlODBC and its XA library open further connections of their own to finish the transaction. These connections did not keep the security settings of the application's connection:

- When the XA library's first connection attempt failed, it tried again with sslmode=allow, even for a data source configured with sslmode=verify-full or verify-ca.

An attacker on the network path between the MSDTC host and the PostgreSQL server, without a certificate or credentials, can make those connections go to a server of their choosing without TLS, read and change what they send, and decide the outcome MSDTC records for the transaction.

CVE-2026-79751.title: SportEase profile update permits class representative self-assignment through user-controlled class_id
CVE-2026-79751.description: SportEase is a web application for managing school sports events, class rosters, and competition teams. Prior to 1.3, an authenticated account with is_profile_complete=false can submit an attacker-selected class_id for any class in the currently active event to PUT /api/user/profile during first profile completion. AuthHandler.UpdateProfile accepts the class without validating the user's legitimate membership and automatically derives and assigns the corresponding {class_name}_rep role while isFirstCompletion is true. The attacker can become representative of one selected class, view roster information including email addresses, and add or remove competition-team assignments. Downstream handlers correctly reject access to other classes, so the impact is bounded to the selected class, but the representative privilege cannot be revoked through the exposed API and requires direct database intervention or another out-of-band remediation method. This issue is fixed in version 1.3.

CVE-2026-99537.title: ksmbd: preserve unreadable named streams on open
CVE-2026-99537.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: preserve unreadable named streams on open

A write-only client can open an existing named stream with FILE_OPEN_IF
without permission to read the underlying file. The case-insensitive
lookup finds the xattr name, but querying its value length then fails
with -EACCES. smb2_set_stream_name_xattr() treats every negative result
as a missing stream and replaces the existing xattr with an empty value.

A failed xattr list is not proof that the stream is absent either:
for example, -ENOMEM can lead to the same empty replacement. Preserve
listing errors and create a stream only for -ENOENT or -ENODATA. The
latter can occur if the xattr is removed between listing its name and
querying its value. Return other lookup errors without changing the
stream.

A write-only FILE_OPEN now reports access denied instead of name not
found. FILE_OVERWRITE_IF and FILE_SUPERSEDE on an unreadable stream
also fail instead of appearing…

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: deny access for an empty DACL instead of granting the request

smb_check_perm_dacl() returns the access mask it computes to the SMB2
CREATE handler, which uses it as the granted access for the open. For a
security descriptor whose DACL is present but contains no ACEs, the
function is supposed to deny access: an empty (non-NULL) DACL grants no
access to anyone except the object owner's implicit READ_CONTROL and
WRITE_DAC (MS-DTYP 2.4.5).

The empty-DACL branch only denies when both

- the DACL has no trailing bytes (pdacl_size == sizeof(struct smb_acl)),
and
- the request contains bits beyond READ_CONTROL / WRITE_DAC.

CVE-2026-99766.title: scsi: aic79xx: Fix NULL pointer dereference in device reset
CVE-2026-99766.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

scsi: aic79xx: Fix NULL pointer dereference in device reset

Since commit c67e63800446 ("scsi: aic79xx: Do not reference SCSI command
when resetting device") the device reset SCB has no SCSI command, but
ahd_linux_dev_reset() still sets its residual, and ahd_abort_scbs(), which
completes it, sets its status. Seen on an AIC-7902 when a failing disk
triggered a device reset, which killed the SCSI error handler:

BUG: kernel NULL pointer dereference, address: 0000009c
EIP: ahd_linux_dev_reset.cold+0xee/0x26e

Add NULL command checks to the accessors in aic79xx_osm.h. Also skip
autosense for an SCB without a command and complete it with ahd_done()
right away: the REQUEST SENSE path can clear SCB_DEVICE_RESET, after which
ahd_done() would dereference the missing command.
